skill.name: ddd-strategic-design
skill.description: Design DDD strategic artifacts including subdomains, bounded contexts, and ubiquitous language for complex business domains.
skill.summary: Map complex business domains into clear subdomains, bounded contexts, shared language, and ownership decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Complex domains often produce unclear service boundaries, inconsistent terms, and disputed ownership. This skill creates subdomain maps, context catalogs, glossaries, and documented boundary decisions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies business capabilities as core, supporting, or generic subdomains.
Proposes bounded contexts based on consistency needs, responsibilities, and ownership.
Creates a bounded context catalog with upstream dependencies and downstream consumers.
Builds a ubiquitous language glossary with canonical terms, definitions, contexts, and anti-terms.
Documents boundary decisions and rationale for later architecture decision records.
limitations: It cannot determine business truth without input from domain experts and stakeholders.
It does not produce executable code or tactical implementation patterns.
Its proposed boundaries require validation against real workflows, ownership, and consistency requirements.
It does not replace detailed tactical design before implementation.

use_cases.title: Decompose a monolith
use_cases.description: Identify subdomains and bounded contexts before separating a monolithic application into independently owned services.

use_cases.title: Align team ownership
use_cases.description: Connect domain responsibilities, dependencies, and context boundaries to accountable engineering teams.

use_cases.title: Standardize domain language
use_cases.description: Create canonical definitions and expose terms that mean different things across business contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Classify subdomains
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these business capabilities as core, supporting, or generic subdomains: [capabilities]. Explain each classification and identify missing stakeholder information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a strategic design exercise with a known capability list.

prompt_templates.title: Define bounded contexts
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose bounded contexts for [domain]. For each context, describe its responsibility, owner, consistency boundary, upstream dependencies, and downstream consumers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn domain capabilities into explicit architectural boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a shared glossary
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ubiquitous language glossary from [domain notes]. Include canonical terms, definitions, owning contexts, ambiguous synonyms, and anti-terms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve inconsistent terminology across teams and workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Design the domain landscape
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [business description] and produce a subdomain table, bounded context catalog, glossary, team ownership proposal, and boundary decisions with rationale. State assumptions and conflicts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a complete strategic design package for stakeholder review.

output_examples.input: Classify pricing, identity, search, and checkout for a retail platform.
output: Pricing: Core, because pricing strategy can create differentiated business value.
Identity: Supporting, because it enables commerce without defining the retail advantage.
Search: Classification needs stakeholder evidence about differentiation and customer value.
Checkout: Supporting or core, depending on whether the purchase experience creates measurable advantage.

output_examples.input: Separate the meanings of order across checkout and fulfillment.
output: Checkout Order: A confirmed purchase request accepted after payment authorization.
Fulfillment Order: An operational instruction to reserve, pack, and dispatch purchased items.
Boundary decision: Each context owns its definition and translates the term at integration points.

best_practices: Provide real business capabilities, workflows, constraints, and current ownership before requesting boundaries.
Validate every classification and term with domain experts from the affected contexts.
Record assumptions and unresolved conflicts beside each proposed boundary decision.
anti_patterns: Do not treat technical layers or database tables as business subdomains.
Do not force one universal definition when a term has valid context-specific meanings.
Do not implement proposed boundaries before stakeholders validate responsibilities and ownership.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide business capabilities, important workflows, domain terms, current systems, team ownership, dependencies, and known consistency requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill generate implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It produces strategic design artifacts that should guide later tactical design and implementation.

faq.question: Can it classify a subdomain without stakeholder input?
faq.answer: It can propose a classification, but domain experts must validate business differentiation, value, and operational importance.

faq.question: How are bounded contexts selected?
faq.answer: The skill considers responsibilities, consistency needs, ownership, dependencies, and differences in domain language.

faq.question: Can it help split a monolith?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose domain boundaries and ownership before teams choose technical extraction strategies.

faq.question: What should happen after strategic design?
faq.answer: Validate the artifacts, record boundary decisions, then perform tactical design for aggregates, events, interfaces, and implementation details.
